old: It began as a wax seal pressed onto an official document, long before it meant paper you owe money on.
Its Latin ancestor, bulla, meant a seal or sealed document.
It shares that Latin root with the word for a papal bull — both came from the same sealed-document sense.
clues: This common written document traces back to a Latin word for a seal, and it first named an official paper stamped shut with wax.
It's the statement a restaurant, shop or utility company gives you showing what you owe, unlike a receipt, which proves you've already paid.
Lawmakers vote on one before it becomes law, you can pay with a five-dollar one, and it shares its Latin seal root with a pope's decree called a bull.
